7. Fees and Reimbursable Expenses
As this engagement will be structured as a lump-sum contract, the selected Consultant shall submit a financial
proposal (in addition to a technical proposal) that includes:
A total lump-sum price for the performance of the services, payable against the deliverables set
out in Section VIII, supported by a breakdown of professional fees by each proposed expert and
personnel category, indicating the applicable unit rates and estimated level of effort (person-months
or person-days), provided for information purposes; and

14
Reimbursable expenses, included within the lump-sum price, covering any anticipated travel,
accommodation, per diem, logistics, communications, and other project-related costs necessary for
the performance of the services.

The lump-sum price shall be inclusive of all costs necessary for the performance of the services. The Consultant
shall clearly state the assumptions underlying the proposed costs and provide sufficient detail to allow MEC to
assess the reasonableness of the proposed budget.
8. Deliverables
The project has six (6) main deliverables.
The Consultant shall prepare and submit the following deliverables in accordance with the Scope of Services.
The Task references identify the principal Tasks contributing to each deliverable and shall not limit the
Consultant's obligation to take into account relevant findings and recommendations arising from other Tasks.
1. Deliverable 1: Inception Report (Linked to: Tasks 1 to 7)
The Consultant shall submit an Inception Report confirming its understanding of the assignment, methodology,
work plan, stakeholder engagement arrangements, data and information requirements, and detailed schedule for
carrying out the seven Tasks and submitting the required deliverables.
An Inception Workshop shall be conducted with MEC, NEA, and other relevant stakeholders, and agreed
outcomes shall be reflected in the final Inception Report.
The Deliverable shall be submitted within two weeks of Notice to Proceed (NTP).
2. Deliverable 2: Diagnostic Assessment and Implementation Roadmap (Linked to: Tasks 1, 2 and 3)
The Consultant shall prepare a consolidated Diagnostic Assessment and Implementation Roadmap for the
relevant provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, relating to
renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e-mobility.
The deliverable shall consolidate the diagnostic and strategic reviews, identify and categorize the principal
implementation, policy, regulatory, and institutional gaps and misalignments, and establish a prioritized, time-
bound roadmap to address them.
The roadmap shall identify responsible institutions, required actions, sequencing, dependencies, priorities, and
the policies, regulations, codes, and guidelines to be prepared or aligned under this assignment.
The Deliverable shall be submitted within ten weeks of the NTP.
3. Deliverable 3: Institutional and Capacity Development Framework (Linked to: Task 4 and relevant
institutional findings from Tasks 1 to 3)
The Consultant shall prepare an Institutional and Capacity Development Framework setting out the
recommended institutional arrangements, roles and responsibilities, coordination arrangements, manpower and
skills requirements, identified capacity gaps, and capacity-development strategy for RE, EE and e-mobility.

15
The proposed framework shall be consistent with the findings and priorities established under Deliverable 2
The Deliverable shall be submitted within eighteen weeks of the NTP.
4. Deliverable 4: Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework and RE Report (Linked to: Task 5)
The Consultant shall prepare the Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework for monitoring progress in
RE, EE and e-mobility, including the recommended database, data collection, validation and reporting
arrangements and institutional responsibilities.
The deliverable shall include the recommended database and reporting arrangements and the first RE Report,
prepared in a form suitable for subsequent updating by NEA.
The Deliverable shall be submitted within twenty-four weeks of the NTP.
5. Deliverable 5: Electricity Tariff Review and Recommendations (Linked to: Task 6)
The Consultant shall prepare a stand-alone Electricity Tariff Review and Recommendations Report, presenting
the assessment, findings, and recommended tariff and regulatory pathway in accordance with Task 6.
The deliverable shall provide the analytical and regulatory basis necessary to support tariff-related decisions and the
preparation or implementation of the applicable tariff and billing regulatory framework.
The deliverable shall also include the updated tariff model in editable form, covering all MEC-served systems
including Ebeye, and concise briefing notes setting out the rationale and supporting calculations for the
recommended tariff positions, for use by MEC and NEA in policy and stakeholder discussions.
The Deliverable shall be submitted within twenty-six weeks of the NTP.
6. Deliverable 6: Policies, Regulations, Codes and Guidelines for Implementation of the Energy Act
(Linked to: Task 7, informed by Tasks 1, 2 and 3)
Based on the approved recommendations and implementation roadmap, the Consultant shall prepare and/or
align the policies, regulations, codes, and guidelines identified as necessary to implement the relevant
provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, within the scope of the
assignment.
The deliverable shall comprise the agreed package of new and/or revised policies, regulations, codes and
guidelines covering, as applicable:
Electricity-sector regulation;
Renewable energy;
Energy efficiency, including air-conditioning and cooling; and
E-mobility.
The policies, regulations, codes and guidelines shall be consistent with the gaps, priorities and sequencing
established through the preceding Tasks and agreed with NEA and MEC.

16
The Deliverable shall be submitted within thirty-two weeks of the NTP.
9. Contract Duration
The contract duration is 9 months. The expected start date is January 2027.
10. Evaluation Criteria
The Consultant will be selected using the Consultant’s Qualifications-Based Selection (CQS) method in
accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and the REGAIN Procurement
Plan. Interested firms shall submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) demonstrating their qualifications and
relevant experience. EOIs will be evaluated against the criteria below. The most qualified and experienced firm
will be invited to submit a combined technical and financial proposal and, if responsive, to negotiate a contract.
Experience preparing energy-sector legal, policy and regulatory frameworks, or implementation plans
for energy legislation, including regulations, codes and licensing (35 points)
Experience in electricity tariff, cost-of-service and revenue-requirement studies for small island or multi-
system utilities, preferably with high renewable energy penetration (25 points)
Experience in the Pacific or other Small Island Developing States (25 points)
Technical and managerial capability of the firm, including core business, years in business, organization
and availability of relevant expertise (15 points)
Total: 100 points
Key experts will not be evaluated at the EOI stage. The qualifications of the proposed key experts set out in
Section 6 will be reviewed when the selected firm submits its technical proposal.
